sentences.translation: Read the Public Signage in Japan
In Japan, there is a short and accurate Japanese sign in public places.
It is characterized by a mix of honorific, imperative and prohibited expressions.
Read the eight signs you see often.
For those with small children, etc.
It is not a compulsory expression, but a polite expression of a request.
tsukuda, your cell phone is in manner mode.
Set it up, do not call.
power up near the priority seat.
Please refrain from saying it" = "Don't do it" politely.
Manor mode" is a mode to set the ringtone so that it does not ring.
wolf, you must take your dog's shit home.
to the park that everyone can use
The expression ending with "~" is the form of written words that indicate rules and obligations.
Let's do it" is a call to encourage action together.
All the seats in our shop are nonsmoking.
thank you for your understanding and cooperation
All seats are non-smoking" = smoking is not allowed in all seats.
In recent years, Japanese restaurants have been required to ban smoking in the indoors.
near the cash register at the convenience store.
if you buy alcoholic beverages and cigarettes
from the screen of the age 20 or older
In Japan, purchase of alcoholic beverages and cigarettes is limited to those over 20 years old.
In convenience store cashiers, it is common to touch the age check button by yourself.
The maximum number of passengers can be accommodated.
Loading volume" = the upper limit of weight that can be loaded.
Food and drink in the building
It is a hard expression and is often used in public places.
The entrance to the parking lot.
The vehicle is moving the tow.
"Lecker movement" = to force the movement of the car by the tow truck.
The feature of parking sign is to convey strong warnings with short characters.
| Please refrain from doing so _ A polite ban
| ^Please be more polite in your request|
